mainTopic: The source of the 'tools in hand' principle in the potter's case, and whether eating תרומה, a witnessed document, or נשיאות כפים can prove a כהן's יוחסין.
overview: The גמרא finishes the donkey-driver case: we suspect the drivers of working together only when the second one came with his work tools in hand. It then traces this idea of רבי חמא בר עוקבא back to a משנה about a potter who left his pots to go drink. Two ברייתות disagree with that משנה, and he explains them. With tools in hand, buyers handle everything and all the pots are טמא. With no tools in hand, nobody touches them and all are טהור. The משנה's split ruling is a no-tools case beside a crowded street, where people bump only the outer pots. The גמרא then gives a second answer to the argument between רבי יהודה and רבנן: they disagree about whether eating תרומה can later prove a man's יוחסין. It asks the same question about a witnessed document and about נשיאות כפים, and in each case two אמוראים disagree. רבא tries to settle the נשיאות כפים question from נחמיה's doubtful כהנים, but the גמרא rejects the proof, because everyone knew those כהנים' status was weakened.

steps.title: The donkey driver came with his work tools
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer about the donkey drivers. The second driver came with his tools in hand, so we suspect the two of working together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a case where he has the tools of his trade in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to an earlier question about two donkey drivers. Here the second driver is carrying his work tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His tools show that he also came to sell. So when one driver praises the other's produce, we worry they made a deal to swap roles in the next town. Without that sign of teamwork, there would be no such worry.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too: the same idea applies in this case
The tools of his trade
In his hand: he is carrying them

steps.confusionAlert: This line ends a discussion that started before this section. 'Here too' points back to the donkey-driver case, not to the potter.

phrases.english: Here too
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier case of the two donkey drivers coming into a town.

phrases.english: it is where the tools of his trade are in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began in the material before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific situation (tools in hand)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן worry that the donkey drivers are secretly working together, but in the case of testimony about a כהן they do not worry about this. That looked like a contradiction in their view.
steps.terutzMaskana: We distrust them only when the tools in hand show both are sellers who might be working together.

steps.title: Where was רבי חמא בר עוקבא's idea first said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי חמא בר עוקבא originally said his principle about tools in hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was the statement of רבי חמא בר עוקבא said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just used an idea from רבי חמא בר עוקבא. Now it asks where that idea came from, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the tools idea was borrowed for the donkey case. To understand it properly, the גמרא wants to see the case it was first said about.

keyTerms.meaning: And where was it said?

phrases.english: And where was it said,
the statement of רבי חמא בר עוקבא?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָא אִתְּמַר דְּרַבִּי חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the original setting of the principle used in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original case where רבי חמא בר עוקבא said 'tools in hand'.

steps.title: The משנה of the potter who went to drink
steps.stepSummary: The idea was said about a משנה: a potter left his pots to go drink. The inner pots stay טהור and the outer pots become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said on what we learned in a משנה: a potter who left his pots and went down to drink. The inner pots are טהור, and the outer pots are טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting the משנה that רבי חמא בר עוקבא was explaining. It is about a potter who walked away from his pots for a short time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the potter was away, people passing by might have touched his pots. The משנה rules that only the outer pots, which passersby could easily reach, are treated as טמא. The inner pots stay טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: A potter
The inner ones
The outer ones
Ritually pure / ritually impure

phrases.english: On this, which we learned in a משנה:
A potter who left his pots
and went down to drink (water from the river):
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The meaning stays the same either way.

phrases.english: the inner ones are pure,
and the outer ones are impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The principle was said on the משנה about the potter's pots: inner pots טהור, outer pots טמא.

steps.title: A ברייתא says all the pots are impure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that both the inner and the outer pots are טמא, which goes against the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: both these and those are impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says every pot, inner and outer, is טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה split the pots into two groups, but this ברייתא makes no split at all. It looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Both these and those: the inner and the outer pots

phrases.english: But it was taught: both these and those are impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the משנה in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the inner pots stay טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא makes all the pots טמא, so it contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: With tools in hand, buyers touch every pot
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר עוקבא explains that the ברייתא is about a potter carrying his tools. That shows he is selling, so everyone handles all the pots.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר עוקבא said: it is where his work tools are in his hand, because everyone's hand handles them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא בר עוקבא answers the contradiction. The ברייתא that makes all the pots טמא is talking about a potter who is holding his tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding his tools shows the potter is open for business. Buyers pick up and check every pot, inner ones too, and one of them may be טמא. So all the pots are treated as טמא. This is where the 'tools in hand' idea comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Because
Everyone's hand
Feels, handles

phrases.english: רבי חמא בר עוקבא said:
It is where the tools of his trade are in his hand,
because everyone's hand handles them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא: בְּשֶׁכְּלֵי אוּמָּנוּתוֹ בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources into different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה seemed to argue about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a potter holding his tools, who is selling, so all the pots get handled and become טמא.

steps.title: Another ברייתא says all the pots are pure
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא rules that both the inner and the outer pots are טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: both these and those are pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that goes the other way: every pot is טהור. This contradicts both the משנה and the first ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are three rulings: some pots טמא, all טמא, and all טהור. The גמרא needs a case where even the outer pots are left untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure (here, all the pots)

phrases.english: But it was taught: both these and those are pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against the משנה in the opposite direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the outer pots are טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא makes all the pots טהור, so it contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: Without tools in hand, nobody touches the pots
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר עוקבא explains that the second ברייתא is about a potter with no tools in hand. He is not selling, so nobody touches the pots.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר עוקבא said: it is where his work tools are not in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא בר עוקבא answers the second contradiction. The ברייתא that makes all the pots טהור is about a potter who is not holding his tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without tools, nothing shows the potter is selling, so strangers have no reason to handle his pots, and all of them stay טהור. But now both options give one ruling for all the pots, so the next step asks where the משנה's split ruling could fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Where there is not

steps.whatToRemember: Tools in hand: buyers handle everything, so all the pots are טמא. No tools in hand: nobody touches them, so all are טהור. This is the source of the 'tools in hand' idea used for the donkey drivers.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a small physical sign, like carrying work tools, tells us what a person is doing. The גמרא then uses that same sign to judge whether the donkey drivers might be working together.

phrases.english: רבי חמא בר עוקבא said:
It is where the tools of his trade are not in his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא: בְּשֶׁאֵין כְּלֵי אוּמָּנוּתוֹ בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and completes the three-way split.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two sources into different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא that makes all the pots טהור seemed to argue with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about a potter without tools, who is not selling, so nobody touches the pots and all stay טהור.

steps.title: When does the משנה's split ruling ever happen?
steps.stepSummary: If a potter carrying tools makes all the pots טמא, and a potter without tools leaves them all טהור, when can the משנה's ruling apply? The משנה says the inner pots are טהור and the outer ones are טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the משנה that says 'the inner pots are pure and the outer pots are impure': in what case can that be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answers it just gave. It seems no case is left for the משנה's mixed ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חמא בר עוקבא covered both options. With tools in hand, everyone touches all the pots. With no tools, nobody touches any of them. So the משנה's split, inner טהור and outer טמא, seems to have no place to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: the inner ones (the inner pots)
the outer ones (the outer pots)
how can you find it? In what case does it happen?

phrases.english: But then, that which we learned in the Mishnah:
the inner pots are pure
and the outer pots are impure,
in what case can you find it?
phrases.notes: Tools in hand made everything טמא and no tools made everything טהור, so the גמרא is asking where a half-and-half case could come from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the combined result of steps 5 and 7, which seem to leave no case for the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the inner pots are טהור and the outer pots are טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two explanations of רבי חמא בר עוקבא cover both cases, tools or no tools. Each gives one ruling for all the pots, so the split ruling has no case left.

steps.title: Pots next to a crowded public street
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about a potter with no tools in hand. His pots sit right next to a crowded רשות הרבים. The crowd gets pushed against the outer pots and makes them טמא, but nobody reaches the inner ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the pots are next to the public domain, and the outer ones become impure because of the crowding at the edge of the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a special case. The pots sit at the edge of a busy public area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The potter has no tools, so he is not selling, and nobody deliberately handles the pots. But the pots are by a crowded street. People get pushed to the sides and brush against the outer pots by accident. The inner pots are out of reach, so they stay טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: next to, right beside
public domain, a public street or area
the crowding or pushing at the edges (of a public place)

steps.whatToRemember: The potter's tools tell us whether people handle the pots on purpose. The משנה's split ruling is a no-tools case where the outer pots get touched only by accident, because of the crowd at the street's edge.

phrases.english: Where the pots are next to the public domain,
and the outer ones are impure because of the crowding at the edge of the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by finding a specific case for the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is about pots next to a crowded public area.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No case seemed to fit the משנה, since tools or no tools gives one ruling for all the pots.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a no-tools case next to a crowded רשות הרבים, only the outer pots get touched by accident. So the outer pots are טמא and the inner pots are טהור.

steps.title: A different answer: raising someone from תרומה to יוחסין
steps.stepSummary: A second way to settle the contradiction between רבי יהודה and רבנן. Their argument about a כהן's status is not about worry over witnesses cooperating dishonestly. It is about whether being allowed to eat תרומה can later be used as proof of יוחסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say that רבי יהודה and the רבנן disagree about whether we raise a person from תרומה to lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier contradiction between רבי יהודה and רבנן. It offers a totally new explanation of their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the argument was explained as a question of whether we worry that witnesses cooperate dishonestly. Here it is a different question. Suppose a person is allowed to eat תרומה. Will people later treat that as proof that he is a real כהן for lineage, for example for marriage? רבי יהודה holds that we do raise him from תרומה to יוחסין, so he is strict even for תרומה. The רבנן hold that we do not, so they are lenient for תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (an alternative answer)
we raise (we use one status as proof for a higher one)
the portion of produce that only a כהן may eat
lineage, proven family status (for marriage and full כהונה)
they disagree

steps.confusionAlert: This is not one more step about the potter. It goes back to the earlier argument between רבי יהודה and רבנן and gives a completely new reason for it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one small leniency, letting someone eat תרומה, could grow into a full proof of כהונה. That is why one side is careful even at the first stage.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis
about whether we raise a person from eating teruma to proven lineage
phrases.notes: He means: if we let him eat תרומה, can that later count as proof that he is a real כהן?

phrases.english: they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the potter discussion behind. It gives a second, separate answer to the earlier contradiction between רבי יהודה and רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing what the argument is about: from worry over dishonest cooperation to whether we raise from תרומה to יוחסין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Their argument was about worry that witnesses cooperate dishonestly, which seemed to make each of them contradict himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their argument is really about whether eating תרומה can later prove lineage. So there is no contradiction about dishonest cooperation.

steps.title: Can documents prove a person's lineage?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: can a document that names someone as a כהן be used to give him proven יוחסין?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the law about raising a person from documents to lineage?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Can written documents prove that someone is a כהן with full lineage?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the question was whether eating תרומה can prove lineage. Now the same question is asked about documents (שטרות). If a document calls a person a כהן, does that give him proven status?

keyTerms.meaning: it was asked of them (a question the scholars could not settle)
to raise (to use as proof for a higher status)
documents, legal papers

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
What is the law about raising a person from documents to proven lineage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 10's idea of 'raising' a person to lineage. Now it asks about documents.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a document that calls someone a כהן can prove his יוחסין.

steps.title: What kind of document? Not one he signed himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what document is meant. It rejects the first idea: a man signing 'I, so-and-so, a כהן' as a witness proves nothing, because only he is saying he is a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say the document reads 'I, so-and-so, a כהן, signed as a witness', who is testifying about him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts working out exactly which document the question means. It throws out the first option right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the man himself wrote that he is a כהן when he signed. Then the only source for his כהונה is his own word, and nobody else is testifying for him. So the question must be about some other kind of document.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? What are the details?
if you say (introduces an option that will be rejected)
I signed as a witness
testifies about him

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say that it is written in the document:
"I, so-and-so, a priest, signed as a witness"
then who is testifying about him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the question of step 11 by asking which document is meant. It rejects the first option.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Exactly what kind of document the question of step 11 is talking about.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the document is one where the man himself signed as 'so-and-so, a כהן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man cannot be his own witness. If only he calls himself a כהן, there is no outside testimony to prove it.

steps.title: The document is a loan contract where the borrower calls himself a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the case is a loan document. The borrower wrote 'I, so-and-so, a כהן, borrowed a מנה from so-and-so', and witnesses signed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed for a document that says: 'I, so-and-so, a כהן, borrowed a מנה from so-and-so', and witnesses signed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from the step before: which document are we talking about? It is a loan document where the borrower calls himself a כהן, and real witnesses signed it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case that was rejected, the man signed as a witness and called himself a כהן, so only his own word backed it up. Here other people, the witnesses, sign a document that has the word כהן in it. That is why there is a real question to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed for... (the גמרא is about to give the exact case where the question applies)
So-and-so, a stand-in for any name
A sum of money (one hundred זוז)
Witnesses

phrases.english: No, it is needed where it is written in it:
"I, so-and-so, a כהן,
borrowed a מנה from so-and-so"
and witnesses signed it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12's question of which document is meant, after the first idea was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A loan document, signed by witnesses, in which the borrower calls himself a כהן.

steps.title: What exactly do the witnesses confirm when they sign?
steps.stepSummary: Do the witnesses confirm only the loan, or every detail in the document, including that he is a כהן?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Are the witnesses confirming only the מנה in the document? Or maybe they are confirming the whole thing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the witnesses' signatures really mean. Do they cover only the loan, or every word in the document?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses back up only the loan, the word כהן is still just the borrower's own claim, and it proves nothing. If they back up the whole document, then two witnesses are saying he is a כהן, and that could be strong enough for יוחסין.

keyTerms.meaning: About the money in the document
They testify
About the whole matter

phrases.english: What is the law?
Are they testifying about the מנה in the document,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא אַכּוּלַּהּ מִילְּתָא קָא מַסְהֲדִי.
phrases.english: or perhaps they are testifying about the entire matter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the case is clear, the גמרא states the exact question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the witnesses' signatures cover only the loan or also the borrower's description of himself as a כהן.

steps.title: רב הונא and רב חסדא argue about the document
steps.stepSummary: One אמורא says the document can prove he is a כהן for יוחסין. The other says it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב חסדא: one said we do raise him to יוחסין, and one said we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between two אמוראים about the question from the step before. It does not say which one holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one who says 'we raise him' holds that the witnesses confirm the whole document, including the word כהן. The one who says 'we do not raise him' holds that they confirm only the loan.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise him up, meaning we give him proven status as a כהן for יוחסין
We do not raise him up to that status

steps.whatToRemember: A witnessed loan document that calls the borrower a כהן: רב הונא and רב חסדא argue over whether it proves his יוחסין. It depends on whether the witnesses confirm only the loan or every detail.

phrases.english: רב הונא and רב חסדא:
one said: we raise him,
phrases.notes: Raise him from this document up to the full, proven status of a כהן for יוחסין.

phrases.english: and one said: we do not raise him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא וְרַב חִסְדָּא, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers of the אמוראים to the question in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is an argument: one says the witnessed document proves יוחסין, and one says it does not.

steps.title: Can doing נשיאות כפים prove a man is a כהן for יוחסין?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: does doing ברכת כהנים in public prove a man's יוחסין? The גמרא says this is a real question for both sides of the argument about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was asked: can we raise a man from נשיאות כפים to יוחסין? Ask it according to the one who says we raise from תרומה to יוחסין, and ask it according to the one who says we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a different sign: doing נשיאות כפים. It then sets up the next two steps by saying the question applies on both sides of the earlier argument about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא discussed whether eating תרומה proves יוחסין. Now it asks the same about נשיאות כפים. It says the question works for both opinions, and the next two steps show why.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them, a question raised in the בית מדרש
Lifting the hands, meaning ברכת כהנים
Proven family lineage
Let the question be asked (according to this opinion)

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
What is the law about raising from נשיאות כפים to יוחסין?
Ask it according to the one who says
we raise from תרומה to יוחסין,
phrases.notes: This is the argument about תרומה from earlier in the סוגיא (see step 10).

phrases.english: and ask it according to the one who says we do not raise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְהַעֲלוֹת מִנְּשִׂיאוּת כַּפַּיִם לְיוּחֲסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from documents to a new possible proof of כהונה: נשיאות כפים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether doing נשיאות כפים gives a man proven status as a כהן for יוחסין.

steps.title: The question for the one who says תרומה does prove it
steps.stepSummary: Maybe תרומה proves he is a כהן because a non-כהן who eats it deserves מיתה. ברכת כהנים is only an איסור עשה, so maybe it does not prove it. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to the one who says we raise: maybe that is only for תרומה, where eating it is a sin punished by death. But נשיאות כפים, where it is only a prohibition that comes from an עשה, maybe not. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is real for the one who says תרומה proves יוחסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating תרומה carries מיתה בידי שמים, so a non-כהן would be too scared to eat it. That is why eating it shows he really is a כהן. A non-כהן who does ברכת כהנים breaks a lighter איסור עשה, so maybe someone would take that risk. Or maybe any sin is enough to hold a person back.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin punished by death (from Heaven)
A prohibition that comes from a positive commandment, which is lighter
There is no difference

phrases.english: Ask it according to the one who says we raise:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי תְּרוּמָה, דַּעֲוֹן מִיתָה הִיא.
phrases.english: that applies only to תרומה, which is a sin punished by death.
But נשיאות כפים,
which is only a prohibition from an עשה, no.
phrases.notes: The ברכה was given to the כהנים, so a non-כהן who says it breaks only this lighter kind of prohibition.

phrases.english: Or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side that step 16 set up.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the lighter punishment for a non-כהן doing ברכת כהנים makes it weaker proof than תרומה.

steps.title: The question for the one who says תרומה does not prove it
steps.stepSummary: Maybe תרומה proves nothing because it is eaten in private. ברכת כהנים is done in public, and a non-כהן would not be that bold. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ask it according to the one who says we do not raise: maybe that is only for תרומה, which is eaten in private. But נשיאות כפים is done in public. If he were not a כהן, a person would not be so bold. Or maybe there is no difference.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is real even for the one who says תרומה does not prove יוחסין. The next step brings the dispute about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-כהן could eat תרומה in secret, so eating it shows nothing. ברכת כהנים is done in front of the whole shul, and a non-כהן would hardly have the nerve to do it there, so maybe it does prove he is a כהן. Or maybe we still worry he might be that bold.

keyTerms.meaning: In private
In public
Acts boldly and shamelessly

steps.confusionAlert: The two sides use opposite reasons. The first side asks whether ברכת כהנים is weaker than תרומה, because the punishment is lighter. The second side asks whether it is stronger, because it is done in public.
steps.whatToRemember: The question about נשיאות כפים is real on both sides of the תרומה argument. It may be weaker proof, since its punishment is lighter, or stronger proof, since it is done in public.

phrases.english: Ask it according to the one who says we do not raise:
that applies only to תרומה, which is eaten in private,
but נשיאות כפים, which is in public:
if he were not a כהן,

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי הַאי לָא מַחְצִיף אִינָשׁ נַפְשֵׁיהּ.
phrases.english: a person would not be so bold.
Or perhaps there is no difference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the second side that step 16 set up.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether doing ברכת כהנים in public is stronger proof of כהונה than eating תרומה in private.

steps.title: Two אמוראים disagree about נשיאות כפים
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבי אבינא argue whether we may treat a man as a full כהן for יוחסין because he does נשיאות כפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבי אבינא disagree. One says we raise him to full יוחסין based on נשיאות כפים. The other says we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Steps 16–18 by reporting an argument between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעלין means we treat him as a proven כהן, so his family may marry into families of pure lineage. One אמורא says doing ברכת כהנים in public is enough proof. The other says it is not. The גמרא never says who holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise up, meaning we treat him as a proven כהן of pure lineage
We do not raise him up based on this
One said (used when we do not know which אמורא said what)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabbi Avina [disagree]:
One said: we raise [him to יוחסין],
and one said: we do not raise [him].

steps.triggerLanguage: חד אמר מעלין וחד אמר אין מעלין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the known dispute that answers the question raised in Steps 16–18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute: one holds נשיאות כפים proves יוחסין, the other holds it does not.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא, who points to the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא whether נשיאות כפים proves יוחסין. רבא answers that it is the argument of רב חסדא and רבי אבינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק asked רבא: may we raise a man to יוחסין because he does נשיאות כפים? רבא said: that is the argument between רב חסדא and רבי אבינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The same question comes up again in a conversation. רבא answers only that it is a known argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's first answer does not decide anything. He only identifies the dispute. This sets up the next question, which asks what the actual הלכה is.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting of the hands, meaning ברכת כהנים
A dispute
To raise up (to the status of proven lineage)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:
What is [the law about] raising from lifting of the hands to lineage?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבִּי אֲבִינָא.
phrases.english: He said to him: it is the dispute of Rav Chisda and Rabbi Avina.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question in a new conversation and ties it to the dispute in Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the dispute of רב חסדא and רבי אבינא.

steps.title: What is the final הלכה?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק presses: which side do we follow?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: Knowing that there is an argument is not enough, so he asks how we actually rule. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question moves from identifying the dispute to deciding it. Everything that follows is רבא's attempt to answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the הלכה (the practical ruling)?

phrases.english: What is the halacha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבא's answer by asking for a practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the dispute is the halacha?

steps.title: רבא quotes רבי יוסי: חזקה is powerful
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי says חזקה is powerful. He supports it with the פסוק about כהנים in עזרא's time who could not find their family records.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I know a ברייתא. רבי יוסי says: חזקה is great. The פסוק says that some families of כהנים looked for their family records and could not find them. They were kept out of כהונה, and the governor told them not to eat the most holy foods until a כהן with the אורים ותומים would arise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his answer with a ברייתא. Here he quotes רבי יוסי and the פסוק that רבי יוסי relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These families had no written proof of lineage. רבי יוסי will show from this story that their earlier status (חזקה) still counted. רבא will use this story to decide about נשיאות כפים.

keyTerms.meaning: Presumed status (חזקה) has great power
The governor, understood here as נחמיה
The breastplate of the כהן גדול, which could answer questions
The most holy foods (קרבנות)

phrases.english: He said to him: I know a ברייתא.
phrases.notes: רבא means he will base the ruling on a ברייתא.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Great is presumed status.
As it says: "And of the children of the priests:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי חֳבַיָּה בְּנֵי הַקּוֹץ בְּנֵי בַרְזִילַּי
phrases.english: the children of Chavayah, the children of Hakotz, the children of Barzillai,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לָקַח מִבְּנוֹת בַּרְזִילַּי הַגִּלְעָדִי אִשָּׁה
phrases.english: who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Giladite
and was called by their name.
These looked for their written record of lineage
and they were not found,
so they were disqualified from the priesthood.
And the governor said to them
that they should not eat of the most holy things
until a priest would stand up with Urim and Tumim."

steps.triggerLanguage: אנא מתניתא ידענא דתניא רבי יוסי אומר גדולה חזקה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא starts answering the question of Step 21 by bringing a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא will rule based on רבי יוסי's ברייתא about the כהנים without records.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי, based on עזרא ב:סא–סג

steps.title: נחמיה lets them keep eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains that נחמיה let these כהנים keep their old status for קדשי הגבול, meaning תרומה, but not for קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: you keep your presumed status. What did you eat in exile? קדשי הגבול. Here too, you may eat קדשי הגבול.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining how נחמיה treated these doubtful כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is why חזקה is 'great': even without records, they kept eating תרומה, as they had in בבל. They could not eat קרבנות, because they never ate those in exile, so they had no חזקה for them.

keyTerms.meaning: In your presumed status
Holy foods that may be eaten anywhere, like תרומה
Exile (בבל)

phrases.english: He said to them: you remain in your presumed status.
What were you eating in exile?
Holy food of the outlying areas.
phrases.notes: This means תרומה, which was eaten outside the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Here too, [you may eat] holy food of the outlying areas.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by explaining the פסוק quoted in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubtful כהנים keep their חזקה for תרומה, but not for קרבנות.

steps.title: רבא's proof: נשיאות כפים does not prove יוחסין
steps.stepSummary: If נשיאות כפים proved יוחסין, people would wrongly treat these doubtful כהנים as fully proven, since they did ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think we raise to יוחסין from נשיאות כפים, then these men, since they lift their hands, will come to be raised up!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא uses the ברייתא to show that the halacha is אין מעלין: נשיאות כפים does not prove יוחסין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחמיה left these doubtful כהנים with their old status, which also included doing ברכת כהנים. If ברכת כהנים proved lineage, people watching would later count them as proven כהנים, which would be a mistake. So it must be that ברכת כהנים does not prove יוחסין.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would think
They spread their hands (for ברכת כהנים)
People will come to raise them up (to proven lineage)

phrases.english: And if you would think
that we raise from lifting of the hands to lineage,
these men, since they spread their hands,
people will come to raise them up!

steps.triggerLanguage: ואי סלקא דעתך מעלין מנשיאות כפים ליוחסין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a ruling on the dispute of Step 19 from the ברייתא in Steps 22–23.
steps.raayaObject: The view that אין מעלין מנשיאות כפים ליוחסין
steps.raayaSupportSource: נחמיה let the doubtful כהנים keep their status, including ברכת כהנים, and did not worry that people would treat them as proven.

steps.title: Their case was different: their status was weakened
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. These כהנים were known to be doubtful, so no one would treat them as proven because of ברכת כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different, because their חזקה was weakened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's proof by saying the story of נחמיה is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone could see that these כהנים were not allowed to eat קרבנות like other כהנים. Because their status was openly in doubt, there was no worry that people would raise them up. A normal כהן doing ברכת כהנים has no such warning sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different
Their presumed status was weakened

phrases.english: Here it is different,
because their presumed status was weakened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from נחמיה's case; it does not decide the dispute either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The doubtful כהנים were a special case whose weak status was well known, so nothing can be learned about ordinary כהנים.

steps.title: Proof for the rejection from תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the rejection must be right. Otherwise, even the view that תרומה proves יוחסין would face the same problem, since these men ate תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, then according to the one who says we raise from תרומה to יוחסין: since they eat תרומה, people will come to raise them up! Rather, it must be because their חזקה was weakened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection by showing that the same question would hit the opinion about תרומה. It closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחמיה openly let them eat תרומה. If people would raise them up anyway, the view that תרומה proves יוחסין would be impossible. So the only explanation is that their weak status was known, and that same reason answers the question about ברכת כהנים. רבא's proof falls, and the dispute stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you do not say this
According to the one who says
Rather, is it not that...

steps.whatToRemember: רבא tried to prove from נחמיה's doubtful כהנים that נשיאות כפים does not prove יוחסין. The גמרא answered that their weakened status was known to everyone. It proved this answer from תרומה, which they ate openly. So נחמיה's case teaches nothing about an ordinary כהן, and the dispute between רב חסדא and רבי אבינא is not decided here.

phrases.english: For if you do not say this,
according to the one who says we raise from תרומה to lineage:
since they eat תרומה,
people will come to raise them up!
Rather, is it not because their presumed status was weakened?

steps.triggerLanguage: דאי לא תימא הכי למאן דאמר מעלין מתרומה ליוחסין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in Step 25 by showing the same reasoning is needed for the view about תרומה.
steps.raayaObject: The rejection that נחמיה's case is special because their status was weakened
steps.raayaSupportSource: The view that תרומה proves יוחסין would otherwise face the same problem, since these כהנים ate תרומה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נחמיה's case cannot settle whether נשיאות כפים proves יוחסין, because those כהנים had a known weakened status.
